svg.aria-label: How to write 谢: 12 strokes · 11 pen lifts · 17 movements
svg.title: Writing 谢
svg.desc: 17 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 谢 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 谢.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E8%B0%A2.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 谢. Medians 1–2 draw 讠: a down-right dot, then a separately started short horizontal that turns down and finishes up-right without lifting. Medians 3–9 draw 身: an upper falling stroke, the left side, a separately started top horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks left at the base without lifting, two inner horizontals, a wide lower horizontal, and a lower falling stroke down-left. Medians 10–12 draw 寸: a horizontal, a separately started vertical that hooks left at the base without lifting, and a final down-right dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all twelve medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, all five internal turns across 讠, 身, and 寸, and eleven intervening lifts; Noto's 身 enclosure is squarer and 寸's hook is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.
